items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] No, I think he used different people like Red Happy, they called him. [INTERVIEWEE] Happy Bolton. Yeah. Happy Bolton on drums, who was the greatest drummer I've ever had in my life.

ctx.x: Oh, I think it was around 1917 at Tulane Gym. They gave subscription dances every Saturday night at Tulane Gym. And every time they could get him, they got him. Yeah. And they got him for everything else they could get him for too. He had the cream of the crop. He had Kidore on trombone, Johnny Dodge on clarinet. And I don't know whether Baby Dodge was playing drums then. He didn't have Baby Dodge on the drums.
No, I think he used different people like Red Happy, they called him.

Happy Bolton. Yeah. Happy Bolton on drums, who was the greatest drummer I've ever had in my life. Maybe some other people too at times. Yeah, there's no question. I'm quite sure that he'd get up different bands. But he had the same group that could play that really jazz sounding style that we were so crazy about. And to us it sounded like, oh, just something from heaven. I never will get over the sensations I had in the beginning listening to that band. It was just something that I'd never heard before.
